newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate sharply up on U.S. data nerves.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate sharply up on U.S. data nerves.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates retreated from earlier highs on late demand for paper, but still ended up 120 basis points at 20.20 percent on Thursday on speculative pressure ahead of U.S. employment data, traders said.
"There is still a lot of speculation, which is what has pushed rates up so high," a trader said.
Overnight rates had reached as high as 20.40 percent during the session.
U.S. employment and unemployment data will be announced on Friday shortly before the Mexican financial markets open.

"The market was under great pressure and although overnight rates held back a little, you can still tell the pressure is there. Rates held back on demand for paper," a fixed-income analyst said, adding that buyers stepped in once rates were considered attractive.
The analyst said rates also came under pressure from a weak peso.
"There was a lot of demand for dollars which only stopped when the market closed," he said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 4.15 centavos weaker at 7.9650/7.9680 per dollar.
Dealers said overnight rates also came under pressure from the June 11 cutoff date for banks settling balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Furthermore, they said, the market was skittish over the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates and Mexican mid-term congressional elections on July 6.
Despite apparent liquidity pressures, the central bank drained 3.230 billion pesos from the market by placing three direct Cetes sales and six repos
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 50 basis points to 21.30 percent.
Liquidity of 1.193 billion pesos was due to flow back into the system on Friday from prior central bank participation.
